text:
[RARC.5.6.1] The **consumption loop** is the processing an engine performs
inside one public call: an assert, a retract, a clock move or a pump. It is
the engine's **single writer**. Every change to working memory happens inside
it, whether the change comes from the integrator's input, an RHS action or a
TTL sweep. It runs on the caller's thread and finishes before the call
returns; the engine has no thread or queue of its own. Across an input and the
pump that follows it, the loop:

idris.name: lcrs_6_2_1__run_steps_called
idris.note: A fixture's steps on the called engine: a tick, a data input through the arrival, a pump; per pump, the verdicts and the calls.

idris.name: ltim_2_4_1__run_steps_timed
idris.note: The consumption loop's inputs and pumps in the fixture's order, each inside one call. A fixture.

idris.name: Rarc_5_6_1__step
idris.note: What a fixture issues to the consumption loop: an input applied, or a pump under a fuel.

idris.name: Rarc_5_6_2__step
idris.note: What a fixture issues to the clocked loop: one of the inputs the clause's next step takes -- a data event or a clock move -- or a pump under a fuel.

idris.name: rarc_5_6_1__run_steps_net
idris.note: The steps in order on the network engine with truth maintenance: the single writer, one event at a time.

idris.name: rarc_5_6_1__run_steps_tms
idris.note: The steps in order on FireLoopTms's engine.

idris.name: rarc_5_6_2__run_steps_ttl
idris.note: The steps in order on Rete/TtlSweep.idr's clocked engine: the single writer, one input through the loop's steps before firing, one pump through its run.

idris.name: rarc_5_6_2__run_steps_ttl_net
idris.note: The steps in order on the clocked network engine, as Fixture.idr runs them.

idris.name: rlow_4_2_1__steps_agree
idris.note: ANY SEQUENCE OF INPUTS AND PUMPS keeps the agreement, whatever the cadence -- the canonical input-then-pump or a fixture's batched asserts before one pump: each input agrees, each pump agrees.

idris.name: Ltim_2_8_3__step
idris.note: The consumption loop's inputs and pumps with the wall step beside them. A fixture.

idris.name: ltim_2_8_3__no_wall_step_is_the_timed_run
idris.note: The inputs and pumps with no wall step between them are the inputs and pumps.

idris.name: ltim_2_8_3__run_steps_wall
idris.note: The consumption loop's inputs and pumps in the fixture's order, with the wall steps between. A fixture.

idris.name: Rarc_5_6_1__event
idris.note: An event entering working memory from outside a firing: the integrator's assert of a value into a kind, or its retraction of a live fact by id -- the input of the clause's assert and retract calls. A clock move is Rete/TtlSweep.idr's `Rarc_5_6_2__input`, and the TTL sweep's retractions are its own; what else reaches working memory from outside -- an answer, a cross-tier arrival -- is not told apart from an assert here.

idris.name: Rarc_5_6_1__event_in_dom
idris.note: The value an assert carries lies in the domain; a retraction carries none.
